This website is **co-created by the entire RaukR cohort** — one fork, one branch,
one pull request at a time. Every page you see was added by a student practicing
their git powers. ⚡

## 🎯 Your mission

By the end of the workshop you should have:

1. **Forked** this repository to your own GitHub account.
2. **Added yourself** to the [Participants](people/index.qmd) gallery.
3. Made at least one contribution to a **shared page** (and survived the resulting
   merge conflict 😈).
4. Opened a **pull request** back to this repo and gotten it merged.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Brand new? Start here
Head straight to the [**Contributing guide**](https://github.com/ninanorgren/raukr-awesome-website/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
It walks you through fork → clone → branch → commit → push → PR, step by step.
:::

## 🗺️ What's on the site

| Page | What you do there | Conflict risk |
|------|-------------------|:---:|
| [👋 Participants](people/index.qmd) | Add your own profile card (one new file) | 🟢 Low |
| [🐛 Bug Horror Stories](pages/worst-bug.qmd) | Add your worst bug ever | 🔴 High |
| [☕ Best Fika](pages/fika.qmd) | Rate the best fika on Gotland | 🔴 High |
| [✨ R One-Liners](pages/one-liners.qmd) | Share a favourite (or cursed) one-liner | 🔴 High |
| [📚 Recommendations](pages/recommendations.qmd) | Recommend a paper, book or podcast | 🔴 High |

The **🟢 low-risk** page gives you a clean, conflict-free PR to build confidence.
The **🔴 high-risk** pages are *deliberately* set up so that everyone edits the same
file — that's where you'll learn to `git pull`, rebase, and resolve conflicts like a pro.

## 🤔 The whole point

> The content here is meant to be quick and fun — a sentence or two each. The real
> learning is in the **git workflow**, not in writing essays. Keep your entries short,
> keep your commits frequent, and don't be afraid to break things. That's what forks
> are for. 🚀
